name: Kirkpatrick–Seidel output-sensitive convex hull
definition: Let n=|P| and h=|vertices(CH(P))|. Split planar points by median x; find an upper supporting bridge (u,v) crossing the split, recursively construct upper chains left of u and right of v, combine; repeat for lower hull. Intended arithmetic bound O(n log h).
variables: n input count; h hull count; u,v bridge endpoints; median split
assumptions: Finite planar points with distinct x coordinates and no three collinear for provisional version; bridge pruning must be reviewed.
limitations: Output-sensitive complexity depends on exact linear-time bridge implementation; degeneracies and lower hull handling need review.
failure_conditions: Wrong bridge, invalid degeneracies or unverified pruning.
computation: Use median partition and prune-and-search bridge construction; exact pruning rules and termination require independent admission review.

name: Pick lattice polygon area identity
definition: For a simple lattice polygon, A=I+B/2−1 where I counts strict interior lattice points and B counts boundary lattice points; B=Σ gcd(|Δx_i|,|Δy_i|) over cyclic edges.
variables: A area; I interior lattice count; B boundary lattice count; Δx_i,Δy_i integer edge increments
assumptions: Simple positive-area integer-lattice polygon without holes; cyclic vertices, no zero-length edge.
limitations: Counting I can be costly; does not cover arbitrary real-coordinate or self-intersecting polygons.
failure_conditions: Nonlattice vertices, invalid polygon or incorrect lattice counts.
computation: Count interior lattice points, sum edge gcd values, evaluate area identity. Proof and complexity need independent admission review.

source.citation: Provisional source locator: Algorithms for Competitive Programming, Pick's Theorem - area of lattice polygons, https://cp-algorithms.com/geometry/picks-theorem.html ; independent admission review pending.
